notes: The visible non-test code matches the reference fix exactly: it adds ParseableDiffPrefixes() to the builder and uses it at every diff call site, and the parser strips any first-component prefix, reads 'rename to'/'copy to' paths, and splits 'diff --git' lines by symmetry. The candidate updated the existing command-arg tests to expect the new configs; the diff is truncated, so it is unclear whether it added parser-level tests for mnemonic or quoted prefixes.

The production code matches the reference: a ParseableDiffPrefixes helper is applied to every lazygit diff command, prefix stripping is generalized to any single component with an empty result when no slash exists, rename/copy-to lines are used as the fallback path, and diff --git lines are split where both halves name the same path. It updates the existing command-arg expectations correctly, but the visible portion adds no new parser tests (the diff is truncated).

Instead of tracking exemplar state on the series, this patch asks the circular exemplar storage, under its lock during head GC, whether the series has an exemplar at or after minValidTime; it covers all three compaction paths, replay and snapshot restarts, and releases chunks exactly once with thorough tests. However, it misses exemplars still awaiting commit (the reference records the timestamp at AppendExemplar time), stops protecting exemplars evicted from the ring buffer, and adds a stripe-lock-to-exemplar-lock ordering that is the reverse of ChunkSnapshot's iteration, plus a hand-rolled releaseChunks that duplicates truncateChunksBefore.

Instead of tracking a per-series timestamp like the reference, it asks the circular exemplar storage whether the series has an exemplar at or after minValidTime, and uses that in both gc and gcSeries. This survives replay and snapshot restore naturally, and chunk release and metrics are handled correctly. The costs are a global exemplar-storage RLock per GC candidate and no protection for exemplars that are appended but not yet committed (exemplar-only appends racing compaction), which the reference covers. The tests are thorough and cover every compaction path, both appender APIs, mmapped chunks, zero and negative timestamps, replayed samples and memory-snapshot restarts.
